newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was generally steady on good demand and heavy offerings.
Retail demand was fairly good for immediate needs and forward interest showed improvement over the previous trading period. HRI interest continued rather slow, except for a few loin items.
Rib cuts demand improved, with the most interest in the retail markets. Chuck cuts were very uneven at the start of the trading week.
Choice cuts were under pressure, while the Select cuts saw fairly good demand both in the retail and grinding markets.

Select and Choice round cuts also were under pressure early in the week, but demand was fairly good at the lower price levels. But as the week progressed, these same particular cuts regained their earlier losses and were steady to firm by the end of the week.
The carcass price equivalent index value of a Choice 1-3 550-700 lbs carcass dn $.58 at $96.67; 700-850 lbs dn $.20 at $95.14; Select 1-3 550-700 lbs up $.20 at $92.38; 700-850 lbs up $.35 at $90.56.
Closely trimmed items were generally steady on fairly good demand as retailers continue to see a value on these cuts. Beef trimmings traded higher on moderate demand and light offerings.
Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were generally steady on light to moderate demand and offerings.

For the week Select and Choice rib primal 3.00 to 4.00 higher Select and Choice chuck primal generally steady; Select and Choice round primal steady to 1.00 higher; Select and Choice loin primal steady to 1.50 lower; Closely trimmed item's generally steady.
Beef trimmings 1.00 to 2.00 higher; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items steady.

Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses dn $.23 at $100.57; 700/850 Up $.15 at $100.04; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up .55 at $96.28; 700/850 Up $.70 at $95.46.

Cow and bull carcass, boneless processing beef, cutter cow cutout: The lean boneless beef market traded firm early in the week as disruptive weather conditions in the upper Midwest hampered movement of slaughter cows.

However, as the week progressed, demand became light and slaughter numbers increased causing boneless beef to trade weaker. Consequently, the lean boneless beef market in the Midwest finished the week generally steady compared to last week.

In addition, demand for boneless beef became light as grinders shifted to alternative beef grinding materials. The 100% lean items traded higher again this week on light offerings and good demand. The increase seen this week was not as great as past weeks. Utility carcasses steady; Cutter not established; 90% boneless beef generally steady in the Midwest, Texas 1.50 higher; 85% 1.50 higher; 75% firm; 65% firm to 1.00 higher.
The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, April 10 was estimated at 81.78 per cwt., up .22 from a week ago Friday.
